effects.body: The finance-first model changes the trade-off for strategic minerals, energy, northern logistics, and worker safety. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

The finance-first model changes the trade-off for shipping, customs, insurance, freight finance, and trusted rules. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

The finance-first model changes the trade-off for repair, overflow routing, bonded trade, and recognition of flexible operators. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

The finance-first model changes the trade-off for systems design, advanced technology, talent mobility, and institutional control. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

The finance-first model changes the trade-off for food, commodities, central rail, distribution, and household affordability. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

The finance-first model changes the trade-off for clean energy, water, environmental standards, and regional burden. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

The finance-first model changes the trade-off for diplomacy, arbitration, public information, migration coordination, and legitimacy. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

The finance-first model changes the trade-off for infrastructure finance, capital, project management, leverage, and displacement. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

The finance-first model changes the trade-off for steel, rail equipment, machinery, industrial output, and worker safety. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

The finance-first model changes the trade-off for cybersecurity, payment verification, data infrastructure, privacy, and due process. The useful question is not whether the proposal sounds ambitious; it is what authority, risk, and cost move with it.

options.label: Require protective covenants
options.description: Accept fast capital only with disclosure, leverage, relocation, or exit protections.

options.label: Demand distributed ownership
options.description: Give up some execution speed to limit concentrated control.

options.label: Reject finance-first control
options.description: Prefer another model even if that delays current investment.

effects.body: A routing system can be safe by excluding uncertain operators or resilient by recognizing more of them before a disruption. Both decisions create risk.

responseWindow.prompt: How should Meridian balance verified routes and flexibility?

options.label: Favor strict primary routing
options.description: Use tightly verified routes even when congestion or compliance cost rises.

options.label: Recognize overflow routes
options.description: Pre-approve flexible alternate operators with common minimum safeguards.

options.label: Prioritize emergency flexibility
options.description: Permit faster temporary routing during disruptions and audit afterward.

options.label: Keep route control local
options.description: Avoid a common routing authority and accept higher interoperability costs.

storyEvents.notes: Industrial resilience brief with labor/civilian cost lens.

effects.body: Strategic capacity can prevent a future shortage and also lock money, labor, and materials into duplicated production. Choose what kind of resilience is worth paying for.

responseWindow.prompt: How much strategic capacity should Meridian build?

options.label: Maximize domestic capacity
options.description: Build strategic supply even where it duplicates cheaper foreign capacity.

options.label: Target only critical inputs
options.description: Reserve industrial policy for the few dependencies whose failure would stop the system.

options.label: Build shared reserves
options.description: Keep interdependence but add common inventories, spare capacity, and emergency guarantees.

options.label: Keep resilience market-led
options.description: Use pricing, insurance, and supplier diversification instead of large strategic guarantees.
